prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a ligand-controlled method for forming aryl-nitrogen bonds

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B022 to B057. Round 1 showed that my own first choice carries a problem I cannot argue away: six members, including the two most sceptical of the physics framing (Aili, Aqvist), say that the in-cell meaning of condensates is unsettled, and I conceded the same point in my own file. A citation worded only for the organizing principle is defensible, but a prize that needs this much careful wording to stay safe is not yet the strongest configuration on the table. B057 has the opposite profile. The mechanism is quantitatively understood (oxidative addition, amine binding, base-assisted deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination), the ligand-design logic is transferable, four decades of independent use make the consequence directly visible in synthesis and in pharmaceutical process chemistry, and Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the general systems, so the credit is a clean two-person split. It is also the one ballot that members from different fields already rank highly (first for Somfai and Zou, second for me, fourth for Aqvist, fifth for Brzezinski), which is the closest thing to a shared first choice that round 1 produced. I treat that as a sign that the scientific case is robust across expertise, not as a count to be added up. The citation can be explained to a broad audience in one sentence.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is the one I raised against Somfai in round 1: the 2010 prize already honoured Pd-catalysed cross-coupling, and a physicist should ask what is a new principle and what is a successful extension. I now judge the answer to be a qualified yes, but not an overwhelming one. C-N coupling needed its own solution to amine binding, to competing beta-hydride elimination and to the difficult C-N reductive elimination step, and ligand design supplied it. Even so, it remains a method prize in a mature area and will look conservative beside degraders or condensates, which open new capabilities in biology. Credit is also not perfectly clean: Kosugi and Migita reported tin-amide aminations first, and a two-name citation leaves them out. Finally, I give up the unforeseen-capability argument that drew me to B022 and B068, and I should say plainly that I am trading some of that for maturity and attribution.

responses.point: Somfai puts B057 first as a general method with clear novelty in ligand-enabled amine binding and C-N reductive elimination, four decades of confirmation, and a clean Buchwald/Hartwig attribution.
responses.response: You answered my round-1 question well enough to move me. The point that persuades me is that the difficult step is mechanistically different from C-C coupling: the product-forming step is C-N reductive elimination from an amido complex, which was the stumbling block, and it was solved by rational ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkyl phosphines) and not by repeating the 2010 recipe. I would like the citation to say 'general' and 'ligand-controlled', and I would treat Kosugi and Migita in the background text as the precedent that established the idea of Pd-mediated amination but not a general catalytic method. If you think that wording is too thin for Migita's priority, tell me before the vote.

responses.point: Zou argues for the words general and catalytic in the citation and notes that B057 has the cleanest attribution but must show why C-N bond formation is a distinct advance.
responses.response: I agree with your wording, and your point that the committee must be able to say why this is a distinct advance is the test I now apply. I do not think the 2010 prize closes the door: it recognised C-C coupling, and the C-N case required a separate mechanistic and ligand solution. I also take your caution about newer fields. Your observation that degraders and condensates may be larger conceptual shifts is fair, and my answer is that the committee should not give weight to conceptual size when the evidence is still maturing. If you think B068 will be mature enough by the final ballot to be the broadest-support option, I would want to hear which approved or late-stage result you would rely on.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B068 first as a new pharmacological principle with a clinical pipeline, and treats B057 as the safer, more mature fallback.
responses.response: I accept your point that B022 is earlier than the evidence supports, and I have changed my choice partly for that reason. On B068, my reservation stands: no PROTAC is approved, and the Crews/Deshaies/Ciulli citation is about heterobifunctional degraders while the cereblon glue story with Handa and Ito is a different discovery. Your own file calls B057 the safer choice if maturity is weighted heavily. I think this committee should weight it heavily, and I would ask you whether you could vote for B057 if the B068 citation cannot be separated from the glue strand.

responses.point: Sparr shares my B022 position and says the claim holds for the core principle of liquid-like demixing but not for the long tail of condensate functions, preferring Rosen over Pappu.
responses.response: You moved me the other way from where you intended. If the principle is sound but every functional claim must be left out of the citation, the prize honours what Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen showed in vitro and in a few cases in cells, and the credit of Pappu and Mittag remains cut. I still think the principle is real and I keep B022 as an alternative, with your preference for Rosen over Pappu, but I no longer think it is the best final position. I would welcome your view on whether you could accept B057 as a joint choice.

responses.point: Chabes argues that one citation can cover PROTACs and cereblon glues through the shared E3-redirection mechanism, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa.
responses.response: I tried to accept this and cannot yet. A citation about turning degradation into a designable chemical principle through PROTACs and glue degraders credits Handa for identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target, but then Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and the ternary-complex work, which made the PROTAC strand drug-like, are left out. That is two discoveries under one heading. I also still think that no approved degrader is a reason for caution, though you are right that I should not make the clinical pipeline the argument. I keep B068 as an alternative and ask whether you could support B057 if the degrader credit cannot be settled.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts C-N coupling as a distinct discovery after the 2010 prize, or reads it as a sequel.
Whether Kosugi and Migita should appear in the citation wording or only in the background text.
Whether B068 will have a defensible third name and an approved degrader by the final ballot, since that could change my ranking.
Whether in-cell phase separation will be settled well enough for B022 to return as a leading candidate, and whether Rosen or Pappu and Mittag should be credited.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: I have no stated ties to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi, Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, or the other shortlisted candidates. I share a Lund affiliation with Somfai and Sparr, which is a colleague relationship and not a candidate connection. My earlier disclosure is unchanged and I do not claim a recusal.
